law: STYLE STUDIES ONLY — extract principles, synthesise new forms. Copying any reference frame, text, widget, colour scheme or ordering, or cloning another project's spec, is FORBIDDEN (enforced by `python3 -m mograph.pro originality <edit.json>`).

references.title: Pure glow typography + symmetrical comparison nodes
references.source: user reference sheet 3.jpg (6 panels, one creator, studio desk)
principles: Container-free hierarchy: a thin context line frames ONE heavy hero word; the hero is the only loud thing.
Light is the container: the hero emits a soft coloured glow that spills onto the dark clothes behind it, so contrast comes from optics, not from a box.
Colour = emotional temperature: cool violet for calm/teaching beats, red only when the meaning turns to a problem/warning.
Two concepts compared = two equal nodes placed symmetrically left/right of the body, the shared word sits between them.
A Latin script accent can contrast a Persian hero once (bilingual texture), never as decoration everywhere.
when_to_use: a single key word per sentence
explicit comparison of two options (A vs B, before vs after)
synthesis: Pick your OWN hero word from the transcript and your OWN palette from the footage (palette.py).
Vary where the glow lives (behind shoulder / chest / beside the head) and its colour per section.
For comparisons design a fresh dual composition: e.g. two light-pools, two morph_shape outlines, two kinetic_titles on a shared baseline, a split-tone grade — never two copied diamond pills.

references.title: Two-state flip (cause → effect) + split stage product comparison
principles: A neutral state first, then the meaning flips it: the same centre label stays while its surrounding context changes (state A text → state B text), so the viewer reads a CHANGE, not two graphics.
The light moves with the meaning: the glow travels from one side to the other at the flip.
Above-the-head title + a thin luminous arc line separates title space from speaker space.
Split background: the plate behind the speaker is replaced by two product/scene panels that slide in while the title stays world-locked.
when_to_use: a sentence that pivots on «اما / ولی / بیشتر از اینکه»
synthesis: Express the flip with YOUR form: text morph, colour temperature shift, shatter_text break, grade key, or a morph_shape — the circle-badge-with-arc-text is only one historical answer.
Split stage: broll mode behind / split_* with your own media; change panel geometry and transition.

references.title: Multi-creator diversity matrix (10 panels, 4 creators)
principles: Every video has its OWN visual identity — four creators, four different systems; diversity is the rule.
Habit/option comparison as two small object cards side by side with labels below (objects carry meaning).
Loupe/zoom window behind the shoulder magnifies the detail being talked about.
A live B-roll window on the chest shows the thing while it is named.
A physical prop (tool) interacts with the typography — the object and the word share one gesture.
Warning hook = environmental change (shattered glass over the whole plate, colour cast), not a sticker.
Sometimes the best graphic is almost nothing: minimal box-free floating subtitle only.
when_to_use: deciding the identity of a new video
a warning or hook in the first second
synthesis: Start each video by choosing a DIFFERENT treatment family than the previous project (see originality).
Objects: one clean 3D prop or cutout per idea; two ideas = two separate, spaced objects.
Warnings: grade keys / dof / overlay textures generated fresh — not the reference's glass crack.
